problem: The answer contradicts the chapter itself. Section 1 calls waste spark one form of distributorless ignition, and Section 2 calls direct ignition the other form, so waste spark is a type, not another name for the whole system. 'Electronic ignition without a distributor' is a description, not a term.
fix: Question: name the two forms of distributorless ignition and one common synonym for the family. Answer: the two forms are waste-spark (paired coil) and direct (coil-per-cylinder); the family as a whole is also called distributorless ignition system (DIS) or electronic ignition (EI).

problem: The caption says each bar lasts 60° but never says what the bar stands for. A reader can take 60° crank rotation as the spark duration, which is far longer than a real spark (typically 1 to 2 ms, well under 40° at these speeds).
fix: Caption: each bar marks the firing window of one cylinder, drawn 60° wide only for visibility; the instant of the spark is the start of the bar. Coil 1&4 sparks at 0° (cylinder 1) and 360° (cylinder 4); coil 2&3 sparks at 180° (cylinder 3) and 540° (cylinder 2).

problem: 'needs one coil and cam phase per cylinder' reads as if every cylinder needs its own cam sensor. One cam sensor supplies phase for all cylinders.
fix: Coil-on-plug fires only on compression and allows individual cylinder timing, at the cost of one coil per cylinder plus a cam phase sensor; waste spark uses half the coils but delivers one wasted spark per pair and cannot trim timing cylinder by cylinder.
